verdict_text:
YES

The script drops exactly the 48 buffers via a fullmatch regex, casts exactly the 64 projection matrices to bfloat16 (through float32, which the spec says is equivalent), upcasts everything else to float32, and keeps names unchanged. All four required checks run as assertions before any file is written. Sharding packs by tensor data size with a 268,435,456-byte limit, flushes when the next tensor would exceed it, and an oversized tensor added to an empty shard is flushed before the next tensor, so it sits alone in its own shard. The index file maps every tensor name to its shard, and tensors are freshly allocated and contiguous, so safetensors will not reject shared storage.
